summary: The assembly combines a shared copper vapor chamber, flattened sintered heat pipes, rear-facing fin stacks, centrifugal fans, package-specific interfaces and a bottom-cover graphite sheet. Three operating modes update airflow, thermal resistance, junction temperatures and estimated noise; animated paths, numbered hotspots and staged narration explain heat transport. Geometry is schematic and temperatures use a lumped-parameter model, not CFD. Your fin pitch is treated as center-to-center spacing, rather than clear gap. Quiet and Balanced use the prescribed reduced power limits. Heat-pipe width assumes perimeter preservation during flattening; mass excludes electronics and chassis. The reference chassis is illustrative and differs from your specified enclosure thickness; clearance and grille impedance require validation.

prompt: Design a dual-fan thermal module for a 14-inch thin-and-light notebook (a system-level assembly, not a single part): usable interior 300 × 200 mm, chassis thickness 15.9 mm, module height limit 9 mm. Heat sources: CPU 45 W (40 × 30 mm package) and discrete GPU 60 W (29 × 29 mm). Concept: one 0.6 mm copper vapor chamber (130 × 85 mm) covering both CPU and GPU; two φ6 sintered copper heat pipes flattened to 2.0 mm carry heat to left and right fin stacks; each fin stack 60 × 10 × 9 mm with 0.10 mm copper fins at 0.35 mm pitch; two φ48 mm centrifugal fans (7 mm thick, outlets facing the fins); liquid-metal TIM on the CPU, thermal paste on the GPU; a graphite sheet on the inside of the bottom cover. Intake through the bottom-cover grille, exhaust towards the hinge. Implement three switchable modes: Quiet (fans 2800 rpm), Balanced (4200 rpm) and Performance (5600 rpm, CPU + GPU fully loaded at 105 W); animate airflow particles (intake → fins → exhaust), numbered component hotspots and staged narration (die conduction → vapor-chamber / heat-pipe spreading → fin convection → fan exhaust), and compute per mode the airflow, fin heat-transfer area, thermal-resistance chain (TIM → vapor chamber → heat pipe → fins → air), estimated CPU junction temperature, noise estimate and module mass.
